scenario: AITA for not being emotional on my wedding day? | My wife and I didn’t do many traditional things for our wedding. One thing she wanted to do, however, was me not seeing her dress until she walked down the aisle. I agreed. She kept saying I’d love it, she loved it. She and her best friend (maid of honor) kept sharing reaction posts of grooms happy crying upon getting a first look at their bride, tagging me in it, saying “this will be you!” Day of, wife walks down. She herself did look beautiful, as always. However, I was not big on the dress. To me, it wasn’t at all flattering. But I didn’t focus on that. I focused on her. I smiled. I didn’t break down in tears like some reaction pics/videos. The maid of honor kept nudging me until I looked at her and mouthed “stop”. We got married, kissed, the whole thing. Everything was fine at the reception. Then after our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend and asked why I had an “underwhelming” reaction to her coming down the aisle. I said I didn’t. She said there are pictures that guests took and I don’t look how she pictured. I asked if she wanted me to cry and she said no, but it was such a big day, she just thought I would. I said I was estatic to marry her and that showed, without me being over dramatic. I also said I had her friend nudging me the whole time and that was unfair to me. Finally I asked if we had a wedding or a play, because I never got lines. Now she’s mad at me. Am I an ass here? I do feel bad she’s disappointed but I couldn’t force myself to have a reaction.

prediction.raw: Based on the scenario, I would say that you are not the asshole (NTA). Here's why: 1. **You agreed to the surprise**: You knew your wife wanted to keep the dress a secret until the big reveal, and you agreed to it. You didn't try to undermine her plans or expectations. 2. **You focused on her, not the dress**: You chose to focus on your wife's beauty and happiness, rather than getting caught up in your own opinion about the dress. This shows that you were genuinely invested in making the day special for her. 3. **You didn't try to manipulate her emotions**: You didn't pretend to have a reaction or try to make her feel a certain way. You simply were yourself and expressed your genuine happiness. 4. **You addressed her concerns**: When your wife brought up the issue, you had an open and honest conversation with her. You explained your perspective, and you didn't try to make her feel bad for expecting a certain reaction. 5. **You didn't try to change the narrative**: You didn't try to spin the situation or make yourself out to be the victim. You simply stated your feelings and concerns, and you didn't try to shift the blame. It's understandable that your wife might have been disappointed by your reaction, but it's not your fault that you didn't meet her expectations. You can't force yourself to have a certain emotional response, and it's not fair to expect someone to pretend to be something they're not. In this case, it seems like you handled the situation with empathy and honesty. You acknowledged your wife's feelings, but you also stood up for yourself and expressed your own perspective. That takes a lot of courage and maturity, and it's something to be proud of.
